title: SES Band 2 Salary: Converting Hourly to Annual Pay Under Australian Wage Laws
description: Learn how to convert an SES Band 2 salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week formula, and compare with the National Minimum Wage and award rates.
salarySummary: For an SES Band 2 salary, the annual pay is calculated as the hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, assuming no overtime or penalties.

faqs.q: What is the SES Band 2 salary range?
faqs.a: The SES Band 2 salary is a senior executive level in the Australian Public Service, set by the Australian Public Service Commission. It is not covered by the Fair Work Ombudsman awards or the National Minimum Wage. Specific figures vary by agency and are not published in the sources used here, but the role typically commands a six-figure annual salary well above award rates.

faqs.q: How do I convert my SES Band 2 hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Use the standard formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time SES Band 2 role, assume 38 hours per week unless your contract states otherwise. For example, an hourly rate of $80.00 gives $80.00 × 38 × 52 = $158,080 per year. You can also check your fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly amount by 2. Our [the timesheet](/) tool does this automatically.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to SES Band 2 employees?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage and modern awards set by the Fair Work Ombudsman apply to employees covered by awards or the national system. SES Band 2 employees are senior executives and their pay is determined by the Australian Public Service Commission or individual employment arrangements. However, the conversion method (hourly × 38 × 52) still works for any hourly rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the SES Band 2 Salary in Context

The term **SES Band 2 salary** refers to a senior executive level within the Australian Public Service. Unlike most employees, SES Band 2 roles are not covered by modern awards or the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Instead, their pay is determined by the Australian Public Service Commission and individual agency agreements. Despite this, the fundamental conversion from an hourly rate to an annual figure remains the same. Whether you are negotiating a contract or benchmarking a job offer, knowing how to calculate annual pay from an hourly rate is essential.

## How to Convert an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard formula for converting an hourly wage to an annual salary in Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If your SES Band 2 role specifies a different weekly hours commitment, use that number instead. The 52 represents the number of weeks in a year, assuming no unpaid leave. This calculation gives a base annual figure before tax, superannuation, and any allowances.

For example, if your SES Band 2 hourly rate is $90.00:
- Weekly pay: $90.00 × 38 = $3,420.00
- Fortnightly pay: $3,420.00 × 2 = $6,840.00
- Annual pay: $3,420.00 × 52 = $177,840.00

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page provides more examples and a step-by-step guide.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

While SES Band 2 salaries are above the minimum, it is useful to understand the baseline. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage increased to $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award minimum wages also increased by 4.75% from the same date. Most employees in Australia are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage depending on the industry and classification.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements. Superannuation is paid on top of the base rate (or the loaded rate for casuals) at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

If you are comparing an SES Band 2 salary to award rates, remember that SES roles are not subject to these minimums. However, the same conversion principles apply. For more details on award rates, see our [pay guides](/blog) page.

## Tax and Super Considerations for SES Band 2 Salaries

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is estimating tax and super. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies, with reductions for low-income earners. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. For a typical SES Band 2 salary (e.g., $177,840), the tax would be calculated progressively, and the Medicare levy adds another $3,556.80. The Australian Taxation Office provides the official rates.

Superannuation guarantee contributions are 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by the employer on top of your salary. For an SES Band 2 employee earning $177,840, the employer would contribute an additional $21,340.80 per year, provided the total does not exceed the $270,830 maximum contribution base. This super is not included in your take-home pay but is a valuable part of your total remuneration package. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, along with estimated tax and super. For SES Band 2 employees, you would typically not check the casual loading box, as SES roles are permanent. The tool assumes a 38-hour week but you can adjust the hours if your contract differs.

For quick comparisons, our [reference tables](/data) show annual salaries for common hourly rates at 38 hours per week. You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026, which is about $108,352 per year—well below most SES Band 2 levels.

## Key Takeaways

- The SES Band 2 salary is not covered by the National Minimum Wage or awards, but the conversion formula (hourly × 38 × 52) still applies.
- Always confirm your weekly hours; 38 is the standard for full-time work in Australia.
- Superannuation is paid on top at 12%, and tax is calculated using the progressive resident rates.
- Use our tools to estimate your take-home pay and compare with award rates.

For further reading, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) pages.
